question: How many tiers of administration are there in the Panchayati Raj Institutions (in states having a population more than 2 million)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are **3 tiers** of administration in the Panchayati Raj Institutions in states with a population of more than 2 million.
 
• The three tiers are **Gram Panchayat** (village level), **Panchayat Samiti** (block level), and **Zila Parishad** (district level).
 
• This structure is designed to decentralize the administrative and governance processes to the grassroots level.
 
• The Panchayati Raj system was introduced through the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992**.
 
• This amendment added **Part IX** to the Constitution, titled "The Panchayats," and provided for a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj for all states having a population of over 2 million.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The 73rd Amendment Act** came into effect on **24th April 1993**.
 
• This amendment aimed at providing constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions and ensuring their regular elections and financial autonomy.
 
• The Act mandates the establishment of a **State Election Commission** and a **State Finance Commission** to oversee the elections and financial matters of the Panchayats, respectively.
 
• The Panchayati Raj system is a significant step towards achieving **decentralized governance** and **empowering local self-governments**.
 
• The Gram Sabha, comprising all the adult members of a village, is a key component of the Panchayati Raj system, ensuring people's participation in local governance.
